samples.summary: Stated Non-Goal in the canonical copy doc is now false and was not updated: document-copy.md §Non-Goals says "**REST v1 / CLI copy.** Not exposed there; the web list is the only caller." This change adds `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/copy` plus `wafflebase docs copy`, i.e. it reverses that decision. The reversal is argued in agentic-office-workflow.md §3.1 and recorded in rest-api.md and workspace-folders.md (which did get a "Also delivered" note), but the subsystem doc that owns copy still tells a reader the opposite. Repo discipline is to fold the change into the canonical subsystem doc rather than record it only in a neighbouring one; the code works as specified, so the cost is a doc that contradicts the shipped surface.
samples.evidence: docs/design/document-copy.md:50 `- **REST v1 / CLI copy.** Not exposed there; the web list is the only caller.` — untouched by this diff, while packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts adds `@Post(':documentId/copy')` and packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts adds `docs copy`.

samples.summary: The folder authorization/move orchestration is now implemented twice. `ApiV1FoldersController.update`/`remove`/`isManager` reproduce, line for line in structure, `FolderController.update`/`remove`/`resolveFolderManager` (packages/backend/src/folder/folder.controller.ts:30-119): the same `name` vs `parentId` split, the same manager check via `isDocumentManager`, the same `assertSameWorkspace` + `assertNoCycle` ordering, the same two `ForbiddenException` message strings. The same is true of the document folder-move block added to `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` versus the existing block in document.controller.ts:254-278/332-362. The invariant-bearing parts (cycle detection, same-workspace check, cascade semantics) are correctly shared through `FolderService`, and rest-api.md §5.8 claims this makes it "one implementation" — but the permission and ordering policy is not shared, so a future change to who may move a folder can land on one surface and not the other, giving a browser and an API key two different answers. A `FolderService.move()` (or a shared policy helper) would have kept the rule in one place.
samples.evidence: folders.controller.ts:78-110 vs folder/folder.controller.ts:85-118 — identical structure and identical error strings ('Only the workspace owner or folder owner can move this folder').

samples.summary: Asymmetry with the web surface left open: `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents` still accepts only `{ title, type }`, while the web `POST workspaces/:wid/documents` accepts `folderId` (document.controller.ts:131-141). An agent must therefore create-then-`PATCH` to file a new document. Outside the 7 class-A′ items so not a spec miss, but it is the one remaining folder-shaped hole on the v1 surface after this change.
